slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
How can Harlow lift operating margin from 1.0% to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost and the FY2026 covenant, and what comes first?
What drove operating margin from 3.4% to 1.0% between FY2023 and FY2025?
How much gross margin can promotions, shrink and private label win back?
Can Harlow keep home delivery and stop e-commerce losing money?
Where should store labor and the store network be cut, and where not?
Does the plan reach 3.0% by FY2028 within the constraints, and what comes first?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO, presenting the margin plan for board approval

Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028; At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028; Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant); No closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; delivery kept in some form
Board meeting, February 2027
Closing the e-commerce service; Broad price increases and new stores; Refinancing or covenant renegotiation

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Fix promotions, shrink and delivery, not wages: six moves reach a 3.2% margin by FY2028
Margin fell mainly through promotions, shrink and e-commerce, not wages
–	Gross margin and e-commerce explain nearly four-fifths of the fall from 3.4% to 1.0%
–	Hourly pay rose 9.4%, but fewer hours per sale absorbed about 70% of it
Promotions, shrink and private label can win back about $14M of gross margin a year
–	38% of promotions lost money; returning to the FY2024 share adds about $5.9M
–	Fixing shrink in the least-staffed stores adds about $3.8M
E-commerce loses about $10M a year; repricing home delivery adds $2.8M
–	Each home delivery loses about $12 after the fee; the fee test kept 98% of online sales
Targeted labor cuts and nine store exits save about $14M a year
–	The proposed 8% cut risks about $7.5M of its $14.5M saving in extra shrink
–	Six stores close at lease end; three repay their $7.5M exit in 3.4 years
Promotions, delivery fees and labor go first, reaching about 3.2% by FY2028
–	Under a third of the first wave's $16M in FY2026 clears the $20M covenant
–	Stretch levers worth $8.4M cover a 2027 wage rise of up to $7.3M
